title: checksum failed with xdrip, miaomiao and Freestyle Libre 2
body:

Android Version 8.0.0
Freestyle Libre 2

Since the FreeStyle LibreLink software does read the 14-day US sensors and uploads the readings to [LibreView](https://www2.libreview.com/Accounts/Login/?lang=en&country=US), I was wondering as for a current (yet poor) workaround:

- Allow a user to store LibreView credentials
- Periodically (every 5/10/30 min?) login to LibreView and obtain CSV of latest readings (some specific POST operation should provide this I hope)
- Use CSV as input to XDrip+
- Per date/time operate just as if it was obtaining data from a CGM directly or by some allowance of a small delay
- Would this be just another package folder for this follower source in xDrip/app/src/main/java/com/eveningoutpost/dexdrip/cgm ?

I am supposing the CSV seems easily translatable into a XDrip+ database.  All that would need to be written is credential storage just as if we are following NightScout or DexShare and the operations to obtain data from LibreView and accurately process it.

Well, for additional info, it is a POST operation to https://www2.libreview.com/Dashboard/ValidatePatientDownloadExport with some of the following headers (I removed the obvious ones sent with a POST):

- Referer: https://www2.libreview.com//Dashboard/MyMeasurements?intervalPeriod=0&pageIndex=0
- Content-Length: 513
- DNT: 1
- Connection: keep-alive
- Cookie: userLanguage=en; userCountry=US; __RequestVerificationToken=[removed]; cookieBanner=1; _LVOAuth=[removed]; userSession=7/21/2019 6:13:22 AM
- Upgrade-Insecure-Requests: 1

And the request body:

- __RequestVerificationToken=[removed]

However, since they pose this behind a Google reCAPTCHA and verification token it appears they have worked to limit it to once per each user interaction.

@tzachi-dar tablet scans fine with librelink

This is great news @ppppd 
[LibreXposed-v1.1-debug.txt](https://github.com/NightscoutFoundation/xDrip/files/3554296/LibreXposed-v1.1-debug.txt)

What you need to do is:
1) rename the file that I have attached to .apk
2) Than install it on your tablet.

3) make sure to enable it in xposed (they have a screen for that).
After that reboot the tablet for the changes to take effect.

last step is to connect the tablet to a pc, and run:
adb logcat | grep -i xposed > output.txt

Wait a few seconds, and then press ctrl c to exit the application.

Make sure that the file that is created is not empty, and send it to tzachi.dar@gmail.com


Next step

@LubomirKovalcik Readings of Libre 2 sensors 20 mg/dL below the finger-stick ones seem to be common, and not being able to set the "low alarm" below 60 isn't really nice.
The calibration limitation you're seeing is being discussed in #1138 - you may perhaps overcome it by inserting a fake calibration (max 20 off) before adding the final calib entry?
